English: Wool Shearing Stand
A basic open-air frame for shearing sheep, providing the simplest means of collecting wool among the Tibetan nomads.
Spindle Patch
A cluster of simple tents where families gather to spin wool into yarn, enhancing textile production for the clan.
Weavers Tent
Larger tented structures where skilled weavers work together, increasing the clans textile output and supply capacity.
Loom Hut
A semi-permanent wooden hut with several looms, allowing the clan to process greater quantities of wool into valuable cloth.
Dye Pavilion
A large, colorful pavilion where natural dyes are prepared and applied to wool, producing more valuable textiles and attracting traders.
Textile Chamber
A fortified yurt-chamber where woolen products are stored, worked, and traded, greatly expanding the clans economic and logistic power.
Fine Cloth Hall
A grand hall of tented and semi-permanent structures where the finest Tibetan cloth is produced, attracting caravans and boosting clan prestige.
Guild Pavilion
A prestigious guild tent complex, centralizing skilled craftsmen and regulating trade, further boosting the clans wealth and unity.
Master Weavers Room
A private enclosure for the most skilled weavers, producing legendary textiles and greatly improving clan influence and trade.
Tibetan Wool Guild

The ultimate seat of textile mastery: a complex of tents, halls, and trading posts representing the heart of the Tibetan wool trade, granting unrivaled economic, social, and political power to the clan.
